articles.title: Then & Now: Dayton Road in 1993 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.

Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal. A 1993 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Dayton Road from the corner of Calder Road.

articles.title: Budget Hearing Draws 40 Residents
articles.deck: The vote came after 40 residents spoke at Thursday’s session.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Residents of Lower Millrace said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
Public works estimates the work will take about 40 weeks once it starts in January. Councilmember Gloria Lindqvist asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $18,500.

body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. To the editor: I have lived on Vine Court for 5 years, and I want to say what a difference the Foundry Row Mutual Aid Group has made.
